title: Stabilization of the chain A[f^n] exhibits the pro-object A/(f^n) and the pro-object of the multiplication maps as isomorphic in the derived category
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: The lemma assumes a ring A and f in A such that the chain A[f^c] = A[f^{c+1}] = ... stabilizes from some c >= 1 on, and asserts that for every n >= 1 there are maps (A --f^n--> A) -> A/(f^n) and A/(f^{n+c}) -> (A --f^n--> A) in D(A) inducing an isomorphism of the pro-objects {A/(f^n)} and {(f^n : A -> A)} (source lines 26781-26793). The proof has to build the second arrow from a commuting square involving the quotient A/A[f^c] and the multiplication maps f^{n+c}, f^n (proof lines 26795-26803), and then use injectivity of the top horizontal arrow to see that the complex in the top row is quasi-isomorphic to A/f^{n+c}A (proof lines 26804-26805). The author then states that the calculation of the compositions needed to conclude the pro-object statement is omitted, which is where the actual verification of the isomorphism of pro-systems lies.
